name: Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea
native: រដ្ឋាភិបាលសម្ព័ន្ធកម្ពុជាប្រជាធិបតេយ្យ (Rāṭṭhāphibāl sampŭnth Kampuchea Prachéathippatéyy)

predecessors.name: Democratic Kampuchea (Khmer Rouge)
predecessors.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

capitals.name: Phnom Penh (claimed; held by the People's Republic of Kampuchea)

ledger.x: 1979: the Khmer Rouge fall back to the Thai border.

1979: guerrilla war against the Vietnamese and the People's Republic of Kampuchea begins on the frontier; the KPNLF forms in October 1979 and 'operated from several refugee camps on the Thai-Cambodian border'.
1982: Democratic Kampuchea, the KPNLF and FUNCINPEC form the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea on 22 June.
1990: the coalition is renamed the National Government of Cambodia in the run-up to the UN peace process.
1991: the Paris Peace Agreement is signed on 23 October.
1991: the frontier strip returns to the single Cambodian state under the Paris settlement (the page is silent on any handover; the Khmer Rouge infobox shows only an 'insurgency' from 1992).
1993: the coalition is dissolved when the monarchy is restored (CGDK page: 'dissolved 1993'; the people-s-republic-of-kampuchea dossier gives September 1993).

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War
wars.outcome: The resistance survived on the Thai frontier through the 1984-85 dry-season offensive and the 1989 Vietnamese withdrawal; the Paris Peace Agreement followed on 23 October 1991.

wars.name: Khmer Rouge attack on Pailin
wars.outcome: Attacked 17 September 1989 by the 320th and 412th Khmer Rouge divisions against one government division; the Khmer Rouge claimed victory on 24 October 1989.

certainty.note: A guerrilla frontier zone with no recorded boundary; only Pailin is a named place.
